diffuseAlbedo.source: Zhao Ren et al. (2026) 'The mechanisms of color, opacifying, and cracks in celadon glazes from the Southern Song Guan Kiln', npj Heritage Science 14, https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-026-02383-0 (text: L* 'at 60 ± 10', a* -8.49 to -2.25, b* 2.56 to 8.99, all C* below 10; six sherds G-1 to G-6; X-Rite Ci7800, 2 mm aperture, mean of three readings)
diffuseAlbedo.note: Checked: the text gives these ranges and the hue groups (G-4 and G-5 yellow, from more Fe3+; G-1 and G-6 green; G-2 and G-3 tending blue). The value is the midpoint of all six sherds, yellow ones included, so it is greener and yellower than the grey-blue Guan the record names. The claim that a grey-blue sherd sits near b* 3 is a guess: the per-sherd numbers are only in Fig. 3a and were not read. The paper does not state the illuminant or observer, so D65/2 deg is an assumption. The source's range runs from [50, -8.49, 2.56] to [70, -2.25, 8.99].

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/low-iron-glass.json (1.523 for soda-lime float); a ceramic glaze is a soda-lime-alumina-silica glass of about the same index

porosity.source: MuseeVision/Docs/Matter/Story.md, 'Glazed stoneware and fired clay' (a glaze is a glass fused to a clay body, after Kingery, Bowen and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd ed., 1976; a glazed piece is drawn as its glaze, with no open pores)
porosity.note: Checked: Story.md says this. The glass has no open pores. The Guan crackle does open through the glaze, but it is not drawn.

wettingDepth.source: MuseeVision/Docs/Matter/Story.md (a glaze has no open pores)
wettingDepth.note: This follows from the zero porosity. The crackle is ignored.
wettingDepth.derivation: With no open pores, water cannot enter, so the wetting depth is zero.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows.

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
